 Private prison contractors race to get that cold, hard ICE cash 
 by Lisa Needham 
 Staff 
 Monday, November 9, 2026 at 6:30 AM PST 
 Recommend Story

 CoreCivic’s shuttered prison, the Midwest Regional Reception Center, is seen on March 3, 2025, in Leavenworth, Kansas.  AP 
 Sure, we’ve been celebrating just how scared Trump administration denizens are in the wake of the blue tsunami , with some practically leaping out of Washington windows to get gone before there can be any consequences.
 But spare a thought, please, for those contractors who have been lapping frantically at the wide-open spigot that is Department of Homeland Security funding. 
 What are these poor companies going to do now that they can’t make money hand over fist opening concentration camps? Did you even think about them, hmmmm? How are they feeling this week? They’ve been rolling around in piles of money, but the possibility they might have slightly less money to roll around in is just too fearful to contemplate. 
 CoreCivic, owned and run by some of the worst people around, certainly does see the gravy train crashing to a halt. They’ve sold four gulags to DHS for $2.2 billion in the past year, and they have been making bank. 
 Related | You’ll never guess which rat is jumping from Trump’s sinking ship 
 In Minnesota, supposedly the epicenter of government fraud, the federal government spent $495.6 million on an abandoned prison owned by CoreCivic, one that the company had offered to sell to the state for a mere $75 million in 2025.
 Now that’s a profit margin, baby.
 On an earnings call on Thursday, with eager ghouls—er, investors—asking how CoreCivic will continue to make that blood money if there’s a scintilla of oversight, the company’s CEO said, “We would urge the ICE administration to move quickly. They have a need for capacity. We have the capacity. There’s no reason to wait.”
 Yeah, it pretty much is “the ICE administration,” isn’t it?
 The CEO in question, Lucibeth Mayberry, calmed the goblins by reminding them that Congress already allocated DHS tens of billions of dollars, and there’s no reason to think DHS won’t keep recklessly tapping that until it hits zero. 
 Big law firms willing to represent garbage like this were helpfully publishing columns prior to the election explaining that big mean Democrats “have been clear about their intention to vigorously investigate allegations of ‘corruption’ should they win the majority in November.”
 Yes, they did indeed put “corruption” in scare quotes. Well, they should be scared now. 
 David Horsey/Tribune Content Agency 
 A different horrible private prison company, GEO Group, is also racing to get as much money as it can before Democrats take the House and Senate majorities in January.
 During a Thursday investor call, GEO officials bragged that they’re likely to sell more prisons to the government in December, because of course. 
 One of the reasons to do this, on both the goblin and government side, is that making these prisons federally owned allows the federal government to invoke the supremacy clause and say that local and state requirements simply don’t apply. Indeed, that’s the latest trick the feds are pulling: When people say “Gosh, we do not want a concentration camp located in our city,” the federal government just buys the facility instead. Cool.
 GEO Group opened four facilities to hold 6,000 people in 2025, and four more this year to hold an additional 4,800. Imagine imprisoning over 10,000 people who have been dragged there by the government for the crime of being the wrong skin color, basically, and thinking that you are doing A Good Thing and should do it some more. 
 Some other folks who should also be concerned that the money spigot might dry up are companies like Salus. That’s a business owned by a former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem crony, and it got nearly $400 million in government plane purchases in exchange for donating $10,000 to a pro-Noem PAC. 
 Now that’s a good return on investment, baby. 
 These ghouls are making bank off of suffering. A new Democratic-controlled Congress may not be able to stop the already-allocated spending entirely, but they can make the lives of these contractors absolute hell—and we can’t wait.
